brief: Cboe's weekly derivatives note reports the VIX jumped over 16 points week-over-week to a 1-year high of 36%, but argues most of the move was idiosyncratic rather than macro. In a 10-year z-score comparison, equity vol outpaced rates, credit, oil, gold and FX vol, signaling equity positioning, not broad de-risking. Friday's VIX spike, while large, was orderly: SPX's 3.7% drop plus a 3.2-point rise in fixed-strike vols explained 90% of the day's 7.4-point VIX increase, with skew and convexity (downside-put demand) contributing 0.9 point, versus almost half of the November 5th VIX spike. There was no demand for upside calls: little panic, but no positioning for a rebound either. Single-stock volatility (VIXEQSM) jumped over 11 points to a 1-year high of 58% as dispersion rose even though the market fell almost 4%, attributed to investors rotating out of the AI theme into other sectors rather than selling indiscriminately. QQQ vol jumped over 20 points, the most of any global index, while small-cap (RTY) vol, which has little AI exposure, lagged, narrowing the RTY-SPX spread to a 6-year low of 1.4%. Gold fell over 9%, oil neared a 3-month low, and gold implied vol screened richest, near 3 standard deviations above average.
